headline: NYISO IS THE FIRST ISO IN THE PROGRAM TO CLEAR THE T1->T2 RUBRIC GATE: its live T1-F determination is PROMOTE-WITH-CAVEATS (FC-1 PASS 14/14, FC-2 PASS, FC-7 CAVEAT alone), where all six ISOs previously read HOLD. The other five still read HOLD. STILL TRUE, AND THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF: NO ISO CLEARS THE §2.1b FULL-SOLVE AUTHORIZATION GATE, and none opened here. NYISO now reads (a) PASS · (b) PASS · (c) fail · (d) none -- the only ISO with legs (a) and (b) both passing -- and is blocked on an UNRUN T1-X crossover (leg c, chartered as lane D10) and on the absence of owner authorization (leg d, untouched here). THIS REFRESH SOLVED NOTHING AND RE-SCORED NOTHING. It does two things. (1) It carries a re-score that had ALREADY LANDED on 2026-08-25 and that this board was stale by: NYISO's I7 base-year adequacy miss (36 MW in 2026, 51 MW in 2027) is CLOSED by a SOURCED external-capacity accreditation intake -- 2,749.9 MW UCAP from 2026 Gold Book Table V-1, never a number tuned to the invariant -- and the board had gone on reporting FC-1 FAIL / gate (b) fail. Reported with the finding's own honesty note, not without it: the 2026 leg was ALSO flipped by -341.4 MW of epoch demand drift and would have passed by a thin +332.9 MW without the intake; what the intake buys is structural margin (+2.9 to +4.2 GW), not the sign. (2) It applies the owner's SIGNED card-A disposition (A-A, 2026-08-25): gate leg (c) harmonises to `fail` for EVERY ISO with no T1-X run, so CAISO and NYISO move `na` -> `fail` alongside NEISO's standing `fail`. An unrun leg is not a measured one. This CLOSES a leg on two ISOs and opens none; the capx-D1 refresh found the inconsistency and escalated rather than edited it, and the owner's signature is what licenses the edit. ONE THING THE BOARD SHOULD BE READ AGAINST: NYISO's gate (a) passes on the charter's literal test, but its `complete` marker now rests on a NOT-YET keeper (2026-08-25-nyiso-155-hydro-repair) -- the same fact pattern that withdrew CAISO's marker in August. That is owner question Q5, unresolved, and NYISO's lead position is only as durable as its answer. This board is the §2.1b evidence, not a green-wash (rule 1): the lead ISO's remaining blockers are an unmeasured instrument and an unsigned authorization, and they are stated as such.
gate_reading: THE DOMINANT T1-F BLOCKER IS STILL FC-1 ADEQUACY ACCOUNTING, but it no longer reaches every ISO: it is 5 of 6, not 6 of 6. I7 (accredited firm capacity below the reliability requirement) FAILs in FOUR -- CAISO, MISO, NEISO, PJM -- and I12 (reserve-margin band) FAILs in TWO, ERCOT and CAISO. NYISO HAS LEFT THE SET: its I7 closed on 2026-08-25 and its FC-1 is clean 14/14. In PJM and NEISO, I7 is the ONLY FC-1 failure left. The I4/A1 capacity-accounting leak this board once named the dominant blocker stays CLOSED (see honest_unfit 'I4 / A1'). THE LIVE FC-1 FAIL SETS, exactly: ERCOT {I12, I3} · CAISO {I12, I3, I7} · PJM {I7} · MISO {I7} · NEISO {I7} · NYISO {} (none). PJM and NEISO are closest on magnitude (366 MW = 0.24% of requirement, 2030; 218 MW = 0.85%, 2028), though PJM's is UNDERSTATED -- card C's signed hold-last-FPR convention restates it from 366 MW to ~5.9 GW with 2029 plausibly joining 2030, a worse reported result taken because it is the more honest bar (lane S-5 carries it). MISO is the same shape one order larger (6,037 / 3,659 MW). ERCOT and CAISO are furthest and differ in kind: both carry I12 band failures plus I3 scarcity slack, and CAISO additionally fails I7 in four consecutive years (to 9.2 GW) with a 65.5% backstop share -- an administrative over-build, not a fleet the screen chose. PROGRAM-WIDE SCORING INSTRUCTION, binding on every lane that reads an I7 miss (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d2b-i7-ledger-2026-08-25.md §7): NO BASE-YEAR I7 LEG IS A CAPACITY-EVOLUTION DEFECT. `evolve_fleet` is SKIPPED when `fleet is None`, so THE BASE YEAR RUNS NO EVOLUTION AT ALL -- no adequacy backstop, no retirement screen, no entry. A base-year I7 miss therefore grades INPUT DATA ONLY. MISO 2026 (6,037 MW) and CAISO 2026 (6,577 MW) are base-year legs, and NEITHER BACKSTOP TUNING NOR FLOOR RELAXATION IS EVER THE ANSWER TO ONE -- the answers are requirement re-vintage, external-capacity intake and ledger differencing (lanes S-1/S-2/S-3 for MISO; B-1 storage vintage then NQC arming for CAISO). The evolved-year legs (MISO 2027, CAISO 2027-2029, NEISO 2028, PJM 2030) add exactly two mechanism-flavoured questions -- ladder pacing against real exit waves, which CAISO 2027 answers as working-as-designed, and retirement-screen calibration, PJM's open suspect -- and even those sit on top of base ledgers that are provably under-counted (MISO, CAISO) or input-undecidable (NEISO). NYISO's own I7 closed this way: by a sourced external-capacity intake, not by tuning. THE §2.1b GATE, SEPARATELY: legs (a)-(d) are conditions on SCHEDULING a full solve, not on model quality, and no ISO meets all four. Leg (a) passes for the three `complete` members (NEISO, NYISO, PJM). Leg (b) now passes for ONE -- NYISO -- and fails for the other five on their T1-F determinations. LEG (c) NOW FAILS FOR ALL SIX ISOs, and the two reasons are different and should not be conflated. THREE fail on a MEASURED FC-4 that misses its band -- ERCOT (price to 68.7%, co2 to 50.6%), PJM (co2 to 54.2%), MISO (co2 to 75.5%) -- i.e. the crossover input gap was measured and is large. THE OTHER THREE fail because no T1-X has EVER been run for them (NEISO, CAISO, NYISO): no `<iso>-t1x` key exists and FC-4 reads n/a. That second group was split before today (NEISO `fail`, CAISO and NYISO `na`) and is HARMONISED here under the owner's signed card A: §2.1b(c) requires the crossover input gap (FC-4) MEASURED and reported, and an unrun leg is not a measured one. Leg (d) is 'none' everywhere -- there is NO standing authorization, and no ISO's gate opened from this refresh. WHAT THIS READING IS NOT: it is not a re-score. Every verdict quoted here already existed in a committed record before this session; this refresh only stopped the board from describing a superseded one, and applied one signed disposition.
readiness: The FF-3E full-horizon readiness battery is GREEN for all six ISOs — the path is bug-free (input-resolution walk, config round-trip, kill-resume drill all clean; wall/RSS projected). Ten hours of compute today would buy a mechanically-clean but structurally-flawed golden run. Compute is not the binding constraint; the T1-F structural blockers are.

honest_unfit.detail: Adequacy accounting is the ONLY FC-1 family still failing, and it now reaches FIVE of six ISOs, not all six. I7 (accredited firm capacity below the reliability requirement) FAILs in FOUR -- CAISO (2026-2029, up to 9,243 MW), MISO (2026 6,037 MW; 2027 3,659 MW), NEISO (2028 218 MW), PJM (2030 366 MW, and UNDERSTATED: card C's signed hold-last-FPR convention restates it to ~5.9 GW) -- and I12 (reserve-margin band) FAILs in TWO, ERCOT (2027-2030, to -1.5%) and CAISO (2026-2029, to -3.1%). Union = 5 of 6. UPDATED 2026-08-26 (capx-D7): NYISO IS NO LONGER A MEMBER. Its 2026/2027 misses (36 MW / 51 MW, the smallest in the program) closed on 2026-08-25 when NYISO's published external-capacity accreditation was sourced and added to ADEQUACY_EXTERNAL_TIE_FIRM_MW on the FF-2B construction -- 3,168.5 MW ICAP x (1 - 0.1321) = 2,749.9 MW UCAP, 2026 Gold Book Table V-1 with the published NYCA ICAP->UCAP factor. The value OVERSHOOTS the adjudicated 35.7 MW gap by ~77x, inside the pre-declared O(10^2-10^3) band and not suspiciously close to it: this is a sourced constant, NOT a number tuned to the invariant, which is the whole point of the FF-2B construction. Carried with its honesty note (that finding §4): epoch demand drift (-341.4 MW on the 2026 peak) would alone have flipped 2026 by a thin +332.9 MW, so the intake buys structural margin, not the sign. docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d2-nyiso-extcap-2026-08-25.md. ROOT CAUSE FOR THE REMAINING FOUR (unchanged, and still the live one): hydro is dispatched but excluded from the accredited firm-capacity ledger -- `accredited_firm_capacity_mw` reads the persistent fleet, which never contains hydro. NYISO's close is a second, INDEPENDENT route to the same family (external capacity omitted from the ledger) and the cross-ISO check for it is FINDING-capx-d2b-i7-ledger-2026-08-25.md §6: MISO's equivalent intake is lane S-2, NEISO's hydro accreditation is lane S-4. PROGRAM-WIDE SCORING INSTRUCTION, binding on every lane that reads an I7 miss (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d2b-i7-ledger-2026-08-25.md §7): NO BASE-YEAR I7 LEG IS A CAPACITY-EVOLUTION DEFECT. `evolve_fleet` is SKIPPED when `fleet is None`, so THE BASE YEAR RUNS NO EVOLUTION AT ALL -- no adequacy backstop, no retirement screen, no entry. A base-year I7 miss therefore grades INPUT DATA ONLY. MISO 2026 (6,037 MW) and CAISO 2026 (6,577 MW) are base-year legs, and NEITHER BACKSTOP TUNING NOR FLOOR RELAXATION IS EVER THE ANSWER TO ONE -- the answers are requirement re-vintage, external-capacity intake and ledger differencing (lanes S-1/S-2/S-3 for MISO; B-1 storage vintage then NQC arming for CAISO). The evolved-year legs (MISO 2027, CAISO 2027-2029, NEISO 2028, PJM 2030) add exactly two mechanism-flavoured questions -- ladder pacing against real exit waves, which CAISO 2027 answers as working-as-designed, and retirement-screen calibration, PJM's open suspect -- and even those sit on top of base ledgers that are provably under-counted (MISO, CAISO) or input-undecidable (NEISO). NYISO's own I7 closed this way: by a sourced external-capacity intake, not by tuning.
